input.raw_text: Cocoa has gone vertical. New York futures are through ten thousand dollars a tonne, roughly triple where the market traded in the autumn, and every session seems to print a fresh record, obliterating a 1977 high that had stood for nearly five decades. The West African harvest is the whole story: El Niño heat and drought, black pod and swollen shoot disease, and port arrivals in Côte d'Ivoire down almost a third year on year, in a belt that grows two-thirds of the world's beans. Deficit forecasts keep getting worse, grinders are paying up for nearby beans and London sits in a steep backwardation. Exchange margins have been hiked again and again, yet funds keep pressing. Everyone knows parabolas end badly, but with physical beans simply not there I would not stand in front of this.
input.summary: Cocoa prices have risen to record levels amid severe West African supply disruption linked to adverse weather, crop disease, and sharply lower port arrivals. Worsening deficit expectations, elevated nearby-bean demand, steep London backwardation, repeated margin increases, and continued fund participation indicate acute physical scarcity alongside substantial reversal uncertainty after the parabolic advance.

interpretation.summary: The cocoa packet weakly supports a commodity-futures bull-regime interpretation and a sustained-trend activation condition. Its physical scarcity evidence does not establish the statistical behaviors required by the remaining candidates.

citations.text: The filtered probability distribution across three hidden Markov model states (bull, bear, high-volatility) estimated from EWMM features of daily futures returns. The observation vector per instrument is the concatenation of EWMM first moment (mean) and second moment (variance) of returns, normalized and processed independently per asset class. The three regime states correspond to distinct return-volatility configurations: bull (positive expected return, moderate volatility), bear (negative or near-zero expected return, elevated volatility), and high-volatility (extreme variance). The HMM filter produces real-time posterior state probability estimates that can be read as continuous regime indicators. Applied uniformly to 15 futures instruments (4 commodity, 4 currency, 4 equity, 3 fixed income; 4972 daily observations Jan 2000 – Oct 2019). Three states selected via greedy model selection (Nguyen 2021). hmm_filtered_state_probability_bull; hmm_filtered_state_probability_bear; hmm_filtered_state_probability_high_vol; ewmm_return_mean; ewmm_return_variance The asset-independent design is a key feature: the same HMM framework applies to commodity, currency, equity, and fixed income futures without modification. EWMM span parameter controls responsiveness (lower span = faster regime detection but higher turnover; span=30 recommended). Three-state structure identified via greedy approach; alternative state counts were not systematically validated.

matched_states.state_summary: A three-state hidden Markov model (HMM) regime structure applied asset- independently to daily futures returns across commodity, currency, equity, and fixed income classes. The three states are labeled bull (positive return, moderate volatility), bear (negative or flat return, elevated volatility), and high-volatility (extreme variance). The model uses EWMM (exponentially weighted moving moment) features of first and second return moments, normalized and concatenated independently per instrument, as the observation vector. Applied uniformly to 15 futures instruments (4 commodity, 4 currency, 4 equity, 3 fixed income) using 4972 daily observations (January 2000 – October 2019). Three states selected via greedy model selection. The PESR metric (Predicted Expected Sharpe Ratio) translates HMM-predicted state probabilities into a forward-looking scalar risk-adjusted return forecast by combining state-level SR estimates with h-step-ahead transition matrix powers. OOS long-only strategy (Jan 2016 – Oct 2019) achieves substantially higher Sharpe ratios than buy-and-hold across most instruments at 5bps transaction costs (e.g., EQ4: SR=3.0 vs. 1.0 B&H). EWMM span=30 provides a favorable SR/turnover tradeoff (Nguyen 2021 preprint).
matched_states.title: Three-State HMM Market Regime (Bull / Bear / High-Volatility)

citations.text: activity_suppression The smile pattern of TSMOM returns documented by Hurst et al. (2013)—best performance during sustained bull and bear markets, worst during trendless choppy markets—implies that activity should be conditioned on the current equity market regime. Features for regime-conditional TSMOM activity: (1) trailing equity market return over 3–12 months as a regime indicator— directional markets (strong positive or strong negative trailing returns) correspond to the "smile tails" where TSMOM performs best; (2) equity market volatility regime indicator—high volatility combined with low directional trend (choppy regime) signals the worst environment for TSMOM; (3) conditional return decile rank of trailing equity return—TSMOM performs best in the top and bottom deciles, worst in the middle deciles; (4) S&P 500 unconditional correlation monitor (~-0.02 target)—a significant positive deviation signals unintended directional equity exposure that may distort the smile pattern. Do not assume TSMOM delivers uniform returns across market regimes. Condition model confidence and signal weighting on the current equity market regime: increase TSMOM signal weight during sustained directional regimes (top or bottom decile of trailing equity returns) and reduce weight during choppy indeterminate regimes. The 1.8 gross Sharpe is an unconditional average; regime-conditional expected Sharpe varies substantially above and below this level. Near-zero S&P 500 correlation (~-0.02) is the target; sustained positive correlation indicates the portfolio has drifted from its diversifying character. Confidence in TSMOM state returns is highest in sustained directional market environments (both bull and bear, consistent with the smile tails). Reduce confidence in trendless or high-volatility choppy regimes where TSMOM historically shows near-zero or negative returns. Activity suppression is warranted in confirmed choppy regimes where trailing equity return occupies the middle deciles for 3+ consecutive months. Suppress full TSMOM activity allocation when the trailing equity market return occupies middle deciles (approximately 4th through 7th deciles) for sustained periods (3+ months), signaling a trendless choppy regime inconsistent with the smile pattern's optimal conditions. Maintain reduced-activity (not zero) allocation to preserve exposure for the transition back to a sustained directional regime, as the smile pattern requires maintained positioning to benefit from sudden trend emergence. The smile pattern is a conditional average, not a regime classifier with a sharp entry/exit threshold. The practical implication is proportional weighting adjustment rather than binary on/off switching. The near-zero S&P 500 unconditional correlation (~-0.02) applies over the full 1985–2012 sample; within the smile pattern, TSMOM is positively correlated to equities during bull markets (both moving in the same direction) and negatively correlated during bear markets (where TSMOM profits from short positions).

matched_states.state_summary: A market condition in which time-series momentum (TSMOM) signals deliver persistent risk-adjusted excess returns across diversified multi-asset futures portfolios. Characterized by: (1) individual-asset Sharpe ratios that increase monotonically with signal look-back horizon—0.29 (1-month), 0.36 (3-month), 0.38 (12-month)—averaged across 58 liquid futures contracts; (2) a diversified 58-instrument TSMOM portfolio achieving ~1.8 gross annualized Sharpe at 10% vol target (January 1985–June 2012); (3) a "smile" return pattern—best performance in sustained trending environments (strong bull or bear markets), worst in trendless choppy markets—with near-zero S&P 500 correlation (~-0.02); (4) after controlling for a simple diversified TSMOM factor, all managed futures fund net-of-fee alphas become negative under 2-and-20 fee structures (~6% average annual fee drag). Most CTAs exhibit dominant exposure to the 3-month TSMOM signal rather than the individually optimal 12-month horizon, and systematically overweight fixed income. Evidence from Hurst, Ooi, and Pedersen (2013/2010), evidence_tier 2 (practitioner paper with direct empirical content).
matched_states.title: Multi-Asset Time-Series Momentum Trend Following State
